explanation.what: The loop now resumes and waits for every unfinished publish task, and each posts the verdict of the revision its input was created with.
explanation.why: The base aborted every publish task a crash left, so one created for an older target ended unposted. This change resumes them instead, and only the new call is checked against the pull request; a resumed task never asks whether its base and head are still the pull request's.
explanation.fix: Record the target this call validated before resuming anything, and have the task end superseded, posting nothing, when its own target differs; ask the provider for the pull request again before each post.

arguments.failureScenario: Publishing A..H to pull request #7 crashes after the task is created and before its post. The parent lands and #7 is retargeted onto main, keeping head H; the maintainer reviews B..H and publishes. Where the base aborted the old task, the new loop resumes it, and its input still names A..H: it finds no marker for A..H and posts A..H's review, with findings on the parent's code, to #7. Then the new task posts B..H's review as well.
